_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 2026-06-10 00:06:22Z)**_

To keep the program running after each round, you need to wrap your game logic in a loop. Here are the common approaches:

## Option 1: Simple Loop with Play Again Prompt (Recommended)

```cpp
int main() {
    char playAgain;
    
    do {
        std::cout << "After the countdown from 3, when you see the cowboys on screen press SPACE as fast as you can." << std::endl;
        buffer();
        countdown();
        printCowboys("cowboy_duel.txt");
        auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
        char input = getKeypress();
        auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
        auto len = end - start;
        auto timeInMs = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(len);
        int time = timeInMs.count();
        int cpuTime = cpuMockTime();
        
        // Store 'time' in BST here
        
        if (time < cpuTime) {
            std::cout << "You win! Your time: " << time << "ms, Computer: " << cpuTime << "ms" << std::endl;
        } else {
            std::cout << "You lose! Your time: " << time << "ms, Computer: " << cpuTime << "ms" << std::endl;
        }
        
        std::cout << "\nPlay again? (y/n): ";
        std::cin >> playAgain;
        std::cin.ignore(); // Clear the newline from input buffer
        
    } while (playAgain == 'y' || playAgain == 'Y');
    
    // After loop exits, find and display best time from BST
    
    return 0;
}
```

## Option 2: Infinite Loop with Exit Command

```cpp
int main() {
    while (true) {
        // ... game logic ...
        
        std::cout << "\nPress 'q' to quit or any other key to continue: ";
        char choice;
        std::cin >> choice;
        if (choice == 'q' || choice == 'Q') {
            break; // Exit the loop
        }
    }
    
    // Display best time from BST
    return 0;
}
```

**Key points:**
- Initialize your BST **before** the loop
- Insert the player's `time` into the BST during **each iteration**
- After the loop exits, traverse the BST to find the minimum value (best time)
- Don't forget to use `std::cin.ignore()` to clear the input buffer if mixing `getKeypress()` with `std::cin`

Would you like me to implement the full solution with the BST integration?

```cc
#include "../includes/bst.hpp"
#include <stdexcept>

// Constructor
BST::BST() : root(nullptr) {}

// Destructor
BST::~BST() {
    deleteTree(root);
}

// Helper function to delete all nodes (postorder traversal)
void BST::deleteTree(Node* node) {
    if (node == nullptr) return;
    deleteTree(node->left);
    deleteTree(node->right);
    delete node;
}

// Public insert function
void BST::insert(int time) {
    root = insertHelper(root, time);
}

// Helper function to insert a node
Node* BST::insertHelper(Node* node, int time) {
    if (node == nullptr) {
        return new Node(time);
    }

    if (time < node->time) {
        node->left = insertHelper(node->left, time);
    } else {
        node->right = insertHelper(node->right, time);
    }

    return node;
}

// Public function to find minimum time
int BST::findMin() {
    if (root == nullptr) {
        throw std::runtime_error("BST is empty");
    }
    Node* minNode = findMinNode(root);
    return minNode->time;
}

// Helper function to find the minimum node (leftmost node)
Node* BST::findMinNode(Node* node) {
    while (node->left != nullptr) {
        node = node->left;
    }
    return node;
}

```

Done! I've implemented the BST with only the essential functions needed for your use case:

## Files Created/Updated:

**includes/node.hpp:**
- Node structure with `time`, `left`, and `right` fields
- Constructor to initialize nodes

**includes/bst.hpp:**

**src/bst.cc:**
- `BST()` - Constructor that initializes empty tree
- `~BST()` - Destructor that cleans up all nodes
- `insert(int time)` - Inserts a player's time into the BST
- `findMin()` - Returns the minimum (best) time from the tree
- `deleteTree(Node*)` - Helper for destructor (postorder traversal)
- `insertHelper(Node*, int)` - Recursive helper for insertion
- `findMinNode(Node*)` - Finds the leftmost (minimum) node

## How to use in driver.cc:

```cpp
#include "../includes/bst.hpp"

int main() {
    BST scoreTree;  // Create BST before loop
    char playAgain;
    
    do {
        // ... your game logic ...
        int time = timeInMs.count();
        
        scoreTree.insert(time);  // Store time in BST
        
        // ... display win/lose ...
        
        // Prompt to play again
    } while (playAgain == 'y' || playAgain == 'Y');
    
    // After loop, display best time
    int bestTime = scoreTree.findMin();
    std::cout << "Your best time this session: " << bestTime << "ms" << std::endl;
    
    return 0;
}
```

The BST automatically finds the minimum by traversing to the leftmost node, which is perfect for tracking the quickest reaction time!
